original.reason: It correctly derives f(f(x))=4x and verifies f(x)=2x, but uniqueness is only asserted: the claimed exponential-growth contradiction for h is never established. The surjectivity justification is also circular as written.

judgment.reason: The asserted cancellation after applying f^{-1} and changing y to -y is not derived. The resulting identities do not have matching left-hand terms under the stated substitutions, so y(f(t)-2t)=0 is unsupported.
The comparison of the identities at (t,y) and (t+y,-y) does not yield identical left sides as claimed. The key conclusion is therefore unsupported.
Its only uniqueness argument invokes an unshown 'standard consequence.' The described y/-y subtraction does not produce the stated equation under the given substitutions.
The claimed cancellation involving f(t-y) after (t,y)->(t+y,-y) is algebraically false: that substitution instead produces terms involving f(t+2y). Hence the uniqueness step has a material gap.
